senses.def: the top part of the body, containing the eyes, mouth, and brain
examples: She hit her head on the kitchen cabinet.
He shook his head and said no.

senses.def: your mind or ability to think
examples: I can't get that song out of my head.
Use your head and think before you act.

senses.def: the person in charge of a group or organization
examples: She's the head of the marketing department.
Heads of state met in Brussels for the summit.

senses.def: to move in a particular direction, or to lead a group or organization
examples: We're heading home after the game.
He was chosen to head the investigation.

collocations: off the top of my head
note: "Off the top of my head" = without checking. "Head over heels (in love)" = completely in love.

senses.def: a pain in your head
examples: I have a terrible headache from staring at the screen.
Loud music always gives me a headache.

senses.def: a problem or situation that causes worry or difficulty
examples: Finding parking downtown is a real headache.
The new tax rules are a headache for small businesses.

note: Say "I have a headache", not "my head is aching" (correct but less common).

senses.def: the title of a news story, printed in large letters
examples: The scandal made headlines around the world.
I only had time to read the headlines this morning.

senses.def: to be the main performer at a concert or event
examples: The band will headline the festival on Saturday night.

senses.def: the main office of an organization, or the place from which a military operation is controlled
examples: The company's headquarters are in Seattle.
Police headquarters released a statement late last night.

note: Same form for singular and plural; can take a singular or plural verb. Often shortened to HQ.

senses.def: to become healthy again, or to make a wound or injury healthy again
examples: The cut on my hand healed quickly.
It took months for her broken leg to heal.

senses.def: to end a bad situation or make someone feel better emotionally
examples: The leaders hope to heal the divisions in the country.
Time heals all wounds.

note: Don't confuse with "heel" (back of the foot), pronounced the same.

senses.def: the condition of a person's body or mind
examples: Regular exercise is good for your health.
My grandmother is in poor health.

senses.def: the work of providing medical services
examples: The government plans to increase spending on public health.

senses.def: how successful or strong something such as an economy or organization is
examples: Investors are worried about the health of the economy.

note: Uncountable: "good health", not "a good health".

senses.def: the services that provide medical care to people
examples: Many Americans struggle to afford healthcare.
She works as a healthcare assistant in a nursing home.

note: Also written "health care", especially as a noun in American English.

senses.def: physically strong and well, not sick
examples: She gave birth to a healthy baby girl.
Eating vegetables helps you stay healthy.

senses.def: good for your health
examples: Try to eat a healthy breakfast every day.

senses.def: successful, strong, or normal
examples: The company made a healthy profit last year.
A healthy debate is good for democracy.

senses.def: to notice sounds with your ears
examples: Can you hear me in the back row?
I heard a strange noise downstairs last night.

senses.def: to be told about something or receive news
examples: Did you hear that Mark got a new job?
I haven't heard from her in months.

senses.def: to listen to and judge a case in court
examples: The Supreme Court will hear the case next month.

note: Irregular: hear – heard – heard. Hear = notice a sound; listen = pay attention to it on purpose.

senses.def: the ability to hear
examples: His hearing got worse as he got older.
She wears a hearing aid in her left ear.

senses.def: an official meeting where facts about a case or problem are heard, for example in court
examples: The court hearing has been postponed until next week.
Congress held a hearing on online privacy.

note: "Hard of hearing" = partly deaf (polite).

senses.def: the organ in your chest that pumps blood around your body
examples: My heart was beating fast before the interview.
He died of a heart attack at sixty.

senses.def: the center of your feelings and emotions
examples: She has a kind heart.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

senses.def: the center or most important part of something
examples: The hotel is in the heart of the city.
Let's get to the heart of the problem.

note: "Learn something by heart" = memorize it (ezberlemek). "Lose heart" = become discouraged.

senses.def: the quality of being hot, or hot weather
examples: I can't stand the summer heat in Texas.
Cook the sauce over low heat.

senses.def: the system that keeps a building warm
examples: Can you turn the heat up? It's cold in here.

senses.def: pressure or strong emotion, especially anger
examples: In the heat of the moment, I said things I didn't mean.

senses.def: to make something hot or warm, or to become hot
examples: Heat the oil in a large pan.
The debate heated up as the election approached.

collocations: in the heat of the moment
note: "A heated argument" = an angry one. American English: "turn on the heat" (British: the heating).

senses.def: the process or system of keeping a building warm
examples: Our heating bills doubled this winter.
The apartment has central heating.

note: In American English people usually say "the heat" for the system: Turn on the heat.

senses.def: in some religions, the place where God lives and good people go after they die
examples: She believes her father is in heaven now.

senses.def: a place or situation that is extremely pleasant
examples: This chocolate cake is heaven!
Lying on the beach all day was pure heaven.

note: "For heaven's sake!" expresses annoyance. "Good heavens!" expresses surprise.

senses.def: to a great degree or in large amounts
examples: It rained heavily all night.
The company relies heavily on foreign investment.

senses.def: in a slow, heavy, or forceful way
examples: He sat down heavily on the sofa.
She was breathing heavily after the climb.

senses.def: weighing a lot and difficult to lift or move
examples: This suitcase is too heavy for me to carry.
Heavy trucks are banned from the bridge.

senses.def: larger in amount or more intense than usual
examples: Heavy rain caused flooding in the valley.
There was heavy traffic on the highway this morning.

senses.def: serious or difficult to deal with
examples: The conversation got a bit heavy after dinner.

note: Use "heavy" for traffic and rain where Turkish says "yoğun/şiddetli": heavy traffic, not "crowded traffic".

senses.def: the back part of your foot, below the ankle
examples: I have a blister on my heel from these new shoes.

senses.def: the raised part under the back of a shoe, or (heels) shoes with high heels
examples: She wore black heels to the interview.
The heel came off my boot.

note: "Achilles heel" = a weak point. "On the heels of" = right after. Sounds the same as "heal".

senses.def: how tall a person or thing is, or the distance from the ground
examples: He's about average height for his age.
The plane was flying at a height of 30,000 feet.

senses.def: the point when something is strongest, busiest, or most successful
examples: She was at the height of her career in the 1990s.
Hotels are expensive at the height of tourist season.

senses.def: (heights) a high place
examples: I've always been afraid of heights.

note: Pronounced /haɪt/ (no "th" sound), unlike length, width, depth.

senses.def: to make a feeling or effect stronger, or to become stronger
examples: The attack has heightened tensions between the two countries.
Music is used to heighten suspense in the film.

note: Used for feelings, effects, and awareness, not physical height.

senses.def: an aircraft with large spinning blades on top, which can fly straight up and stay in one place
examples: The injured hiker was rescued by helicopter.
A news helicopter circled over the scene of the accident.

note: "Helicopter parent" = a parent who is too involved in their child's life.

senses.def: in some religions, the place where bad people go after they die
examples: Many religions teach about heaven and hell.

senses.def: a very unpleasant experience or situation
examples: Working for that company was absolute hell.
Rush-hour traffic is hell in this city.

senses.def: (informal, rude) used to show anger or for emphasis
examples: What the hell are you doing?

note: Swear word in many expressions; avoid in formal situations. "A hell of a…" = very good/big: a hell of a game.

senses.def: used as a greeting, when answering the phone, or to get someone's attention
examples: Hello, my name is Anna. Nice to meet you.
Hello? Is anybody home?

senses.def: the act of saying hello
examples: Say hello to your parents for me.
She gave me a friendly hello.

note: "Say hello to X for me" = Turkish "X'e selam söyle". "Hi" is more casual.

senses.def: a hard hat that protects your head
examples: Always wear a helmet when you ride your bike.
The construction workers wore safety helmets.

senses.def: to make it easier for someone to do something by doing part of it or giving them what they need
examples: Can you help me carry these bags?
My brother helped me with my homework.

senses.def: to make a situation better or easier
examples: Taking deep breaths helps when I feel nervous.
Crying won't help.

senses.def: (can't help) to be unable to stop yourself from doing something
examples: I couldn't help laughing when he fell asleep in the meeting.

senses.def: the act of helping, or advice or money that makes things easier
examples: Thanks for your help with the move.
If you need help, just ask.

note: "Help yourself (to something)" = take as much as you want. "Can't help + -ing" = can't stop yourself.

senses.def: useful, or making a situation better
examples: Thanks for the advice — it was really helpful.
It might be helpful to make a list first.

senses.def: willing to help others
examples: The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful.

senses.def: for this reason; as a result
examples: The fruit is grown locally, hence the low price.
The data is incomplete and, hence, unreliable.

senses.def: (formal) from now
examples: The results will be announced three weeks hence.

note: Formal. Often followed directly by a noun: "hence the delay" (no verb needed).

senses.def: used as the object to refer to a woman, girl, or female animal already mentioned
examples: I called her yesterday, but she didn't answer.
Give the keys to her when she arrives.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with a woman, girl, or female animal already mentioned
examples: She left her phone on the train.
Her parents live in Florida.

note: "Her" is both object (I saw her) and possessive (her car). Turkish "onu/onun" has no gender.

senses.def: a plant whose leaves or seeds are used to flavor food or to make medicine
examples: Add fresh herbs like basil and parsley at the end.
She uses herbs to treat minor illnesses.

note: American English drops the h: /ɜːrb/ ("an herb"). British English says /hɜːb/ ("a herb").

senses.def: in, at, or to this place
examples: Come here and look at this.
I've lived here for ten years.

senses.def: used when giving something to someone or pointing something out
examples: Here's the book I promised you.
Here comes the bus!

senses.def: at this point in a situation or discussion
examples: Here we need to be careful about the numbers.

note: "Here you go/Here you are" = Turkish "buyurun" when handing something.

senses.def: the history, traditions, and buildings that a country or group has had for a long time and values
examples: The old town is part of the country's cultural heritage.
She is proud of her Mexican heritage.

note: "Heritage" is cultural; for money or property from a dead person, use "inheritance".

senses.def: a person admired for doing something brave or good
examples: The firefighter was treated as a hero after saving the children.
My mom has always been my hero.

senses.def: the main male character in a story, movie, or play
examples: The hero of the novel is a young detective.

note: Plural: heroes. "Unsung hero" = someone whose good work is not recognized.

senses.def: used to refer to something that belongs to a woman or girl already mentioned
examples: That isn't my coat — I think it's hers.
A friend of hers is coming to visit.

note: No apostrophe: hers, not her's.

senses.def: used as the object when a woman or girl does something to herself
examples: She cut herself while chopping vegetables.
My daughter taught herself to play piano.

senses.def: used to emphasize that a particular woman did something
examples: The CEO herself called to apologize.

note: "By herself" = alone or without help.

senses.def: to pause before speaking or acting because you are unsure or nervous
examples: She hesitated before answering the question.
He didn't hesitate to call the police when he saw the fire.

senses.def: (don't hesitate) used to tell someone they should feel free to do something
examples: Please don't hesitate to contact me if you have any questions.

note: "Please don't hesitate to contact me" is a very common polite email ending.

senses.def: (informal) used to get attention, greet someone, or show surprise or annoyance
examples: Hey, how's it going?
Hey! Watch where you're going!

note: Very common casual greeting in American English, like "hi".

senses.def: (informal) used to say hello
examples: Hi, I'm Tom. I just moved in next door.
Tell your sister I said hi.

note: "Say hi to X for me" = give X my greetings.

senses.def: kept or located where it cannot be seen or found
examples: Police found a hidden camera in the hotel room.
The village is hidden away in the mountains.

senses.def: not obvious or not easy to notice
examples: Watch out for hidden fees when you book a flight.
The movie has a hidden message about greed.

note: "A hidden gem" = an excellent place or thing that few people know about. "Hidden agenda" = a secret aim.

senses.def: to put something where it cannot be seen or found
examples: She hides her chocolate where the kids can't find it.
Where did you hide the presents?

senses.def: to go somewhere where you cannot be seen or found
examples: The children like to hide under the bed.
He tried to hide from the photographers.

senses.def: to keep feelings or information secret
examples: She couldn't hide her disappointment.
The company tried to hide the truth about the losses.

note: Irregular: hide – hid – hidden. "Go into hiding" = hide from the police or danger.

senses.def: a system in which people or things are arranged in levels of importance
examples: She quickly rose through the company hierarchy.
The army has a strict hierarchy.

senses.def: the group of people who control an organization
examples: The church hierarchy refused to comment.

senses.def: a long way from the bottom to the top, or far above the ground
examples: The city is surrounded by high mountains.
The shelf is too high for me to reach.

senses.def: greater than usual in amount, level, or quality
examples: Prices are very high in the city center.
She has high standards for her students.

senses.def: at or to a level far above the ground
examples: The eagle flew high above the valley.

senses.tr: zirve, en yüksek seviye; en yüksek sıcaklık
senses.def: the highest level or number
examples: Unemployment has reached a new high.
Tomorrow's high will be 85 degrees.

note: Use "tall" for people and narrow things (a tall man, tall tree); "high" for mountains, walls, and levels.

senses.tr: çok ses getiren, kamuoyunun dikkatini çeken, tanınmış
senses.def: getting a lot of attention from the media and the public
examples: The lawyer has worked on several high-profile cases.
Several high-profile executives resigned after the scandal.

note: Opposite: low-profile. "Keep a low profile" = avoid attention.

senses.def: to emphasize something so people notice it
examples: The report highlights the need for more teachers.
The accident highlighted the dangers of texting while driving.

senses.def: to mark text with a bright color or select it on a screen
examples: Highlight the important dates in yellow.

senses.tr: en önemli an, en güzel kısım; özet görüntüler
senses.def: the best or most interesting part of something
examples: The highlight of the trip was a boat tour of the bay.
We watched the game's highlights on TV.

senses.def: very; to a high degree
examples: It's highly unlikely that it will snow tomorrow.
She is a highly skilled surgeon.

senses.def: with great approval or respect
examples: I highly recommend this book.
Everyone speaks highly of her.

note: Not used for physical height: say "fly high", not "fly highly".

senses.def: a main road for traveling long distances between cities
examples: Traffic on the highway was backed up for miles.
Take the highway north for about twenty miles.

note: American English; British English says "motorway" for the biggest roads.

senses.def: extremely funny
examples: The movie was hilarious — I couldn't stop laughing.
He told a hilarious story about his trip to Paris.

note: Already strong; say "absolutely hilarious", not "very hilarious".

senses.def: an area of land higher than the land around it, but lower than a mountain
examples: Their house is on top of a hill overlooking the town.
We walked up a steep hill to the castle.

note: "Over the hill" (informal) = too old. "Capitol Hill" = the US Congress.

senses.def: used as the object to refer to a man, boy, or male animal already mentioned
examples: I saw him at the gym this morning.
Tell him to call me back.

note: Object form of "he": He likes her, and she likes him.

senses.def: used as the object when a man or boy does something to himself
examples: He hurt himself playing football.
My son made himself a sandwich.

senses.def: used to emphasize that a particular man did something
examples: The president himself attended the funeral.

note: "By himself" = alone or without help.

senses.def: something said or done indirectly to show what you are thinking, or a clue
examples: She dropped a hint that she wanted flowers for her birthday.
Can you give me a hint? I don't know the answer.

senses.def: a small amount or slight sign of something
examples: There was a hint of garlic in the sauce.
He spoke without a hint of regret.

senses.def: a useful piece of advice
examples: The website has helpful hints for first-time buyers.

senses.def: to suggest something indirectly
examples: The CEO hinted that more layoffs were coming.

note: "Take the hint" = understand what someone is suggesting indirectly.

senses.def: the area at either side of the body between the top of the leg and the waist
examples: My grandmother broke her hip when she fell.
She stood with her hands on her hips.

senses.def: (informal) fashionable and modern
examples: The neighborhood is full of hip cafés and galleries.

note: "Shoot from the hip" = speak or act quickly without thinking carefully.
